**Solution 2 is the only one consistent with the checks I could make.**

- **Solution 1 is wrong.** For $n=1$, $\mathfrak{sp}_2 = \mathfrak{sl}_2$ in characteristic 2. For $x=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&a\end{pmatrix}$ and $y=\begin{pmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\\gamma&\alpha\end{pmatrix}$, the bracket is $[x,y]=(b\gamma+\beta c)\,h$. So $\mathcal{C}_2$ is a hypersurface in $k^6$, with dimension $5$, not $4$. The "same as characteristic 0" claim fails.

- **Solution 3 is wrong.** It assumes $\mathfrak{psp}_{2n}$ is simple of type $C_n$, but the derived algebra has dimension at most $n(2n-1)$. Writing $X=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&A^T\end{pmatrix}$ with $B,C$ symmetric, the $B$-block of any bracket has the form $M+M^T+N+N^T$, so its diagonal vanishes in characteristic 2. For $n=2$, $[\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{g}]$ has dimension at most $6<9$, so $\mathfrak{psp}_4$ is not perfect and not simple. Consequently every centralizer in $\mathfrak{sp}_4$ has dimension at least $10-6=4$, not $3$. Since the projection $(x,y)\mapsto x$ is surjective with all fibres of dimension $\ge 4$, we get $\dim\mathcal{C}_2(\mathfrak{sp}_4)\ge 14$, which rules out $13$.

- **Solution 2** gives $2n^2+3n$. This equals $\dim\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}+\bigl(\dim\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}-\dim[\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{g}]\bigr)$ in the case where the derived algebra has its maximal dimension $n(2n-1)$. It matches the exact value $5$ at $n=1$ and the lower bound $14$ at $n=2$. I did not fully verify the upper bound for general $n$, which would require showing that no lower-rank stratum of $\mathrm{ad}\,x$ contributes a larger dimension.

CHOICE: 2
